translations.text: I understand a new topic faster when I can see a diagram, picture or visual example.
I prefer reading or listening to an explanation rather than looking at diagrams.
When learning something complicated, I like to see how the different parts fit together visually.
I can understand a new idea easily even when it is explained mainly through words.
I learn best when I can practise something rather than just read or listen about it.
Before trying to solve a problem, I prefer to spend some time thinking about how I should approach it.
I like learning activities where I can experiment and find out what happens.
I usually need time to think through what I have learned before I feel ready to use it.
I learn more comfortably when a teacher gives me clear steps to follow.
I enjoy trying different ways to solve a problem, even when I haven't been given a specific method.
I prefer lessons where the objectives and sequence of activities are clearly explained.
I enjoy discovering the solution myself rather than being shown exactly how to get there.
I understand a topic better when I can see how it is used in real life.
I enjoy understanding the theory or principle behind something, even if there is no immediate practical application.
Examples from everyday life help me understand difficult concepts.
I am interested in understanding why something works, even before knowing how it can be applied.
Discussing a problem with classmates helps me understand it better.
I prefer solving difficult problems on my own before discussing them with others.
I enjoy learning activities where I can exchange ideas with other students.
I concentrate better when I study or work on a task by myself.
